newsitem.title: USA: AMR Corp still mulling cargo surcharge. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: AMR Corp still mulling cargo surcharge. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]

text.p: AMR Corp said it has not yet made a decision whether or not to apply a cargo fuel-surcharge, a cargo division spokeswoman said Thursday.
"We are considering the implications of higher fuel costs, but we have not yet reached a decision," said AMR cargo spokeswoman Laura Mayo.
AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, had previously planned to implement a 4.3 percent surcharge on July 1, but cancelled that plan when no other carriers followed.
(Corrects to clarify plan was for 4.3 percent surcharge, not 4.3 cents per gallon)
Some European airlines expected to raise cargo rates on certain routes from November 4 to offset rising jet fuel costs.
